prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: Base editing turns a defined chemical reaction, cytidine or adenosine deamination, into a programmable and precise genome edit that avoids double-strand breaks and their repair-driven mutagenesis. That is the kind of discovery I value: a biological process converted into a controllable chemical event, plus a general tool that thousands of laboratories adopted. The evolved TadA deaminase for A-to-G editing is real enzyme chemistry, not just a fusion of existing parts. The method is independently reproduced across cells and animals, its outcome spectrum is well characterised, and clinical use has begun. I ranked it first in my opening ballot and I still do.
statement.case_against: The method dates only to 2016-2017, and clinical proof is still early, so a prize now rests on tool impact more than on delivered medicines. The independent Kondo and Nishida deaminase-fusion work is a genuine competing claim that a one-person citation does not resolve. Overlap with the CRISPR-Cas9 prize of 2020 and with the prime-editing line may also lead some to say the genome-editing area is already honoured. Finally, a prize built on one person's laboratory risks looking narrow beside broader and older candidates.

responses.point: Liu is the clear intellectual driver of both base editors, so a prize should go to Liu alone, which keeps it simple and avoids dividing credit with the 2020 CRISPR prize; PROTAC timing is somewhat early.
responses.response: I accept this and have moved from my opening three-name set to Liu alone. Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments, but the conception and the long programme belong to Liu, and a prize that credits only the first-author trainees of one group is hard to defend against Kondo and Nishida's claim. I share your timing concern about PROTACs, but I would not discount B066 on that ground alone: the cereblon and glue half is already medicine, which is why I keep it as my first alternative rather than dropping it.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a clear and general mechanistic principle with enormous practical reach, mature and arguably late, ranked first by the chair.
responses.response: I agree that the mechanism is clean and the adoption is beyond dispute. My reservation is that this is a refinement of a prize-winning area: the 2010 cross-coupling prize already honoured the Pd catalytic cycle, and C-N coupling is an extension of it. Base editing offers a new capability that was not previously available at all. If the committee prefers a mature and uncontested achievement, I would support B039 as a second part, but I would not rank it above B062 on novelty.

responses.point: Biomolecular condensates reframe cellular organisation as a thermodynamic, multivalent phase-separation phenomenon, with more than a decade of confirmation; the core concept is secure even if details are still debated.
responses.response: I take the concept seriously, and Hyman and Brangwynne's P-granule result was a real surprise. But as an experimentalist I distinguish the secure concept from the claims built on it. Many in vitro droplet results used non-physiological concentrations, and in-cell evidence that a given condensate is liquid and functional has often been indirect. I would want the committee to be able to name the chemical principle that is settled. Until then I rank it below base editing, and I would not credit more than Hyman and Brangwynne because the attribution beyond them is unresolved.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation, through PROTACs and cereblon-mediated molecular glues, is a programmable drug modality and the right first choice, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as laureates.
responses.response: I agree this is the strongest broad candidate, with six of eight members ranking it, and I proposed the same three names. We differ on rank: no PROTAC has been approved, and the concept and the glue mechanism are two different stories that a single citation must combine. I would be comfortable with B066 as the prize if the committee shares your confidence about timing, but I think base editing is cleaner as a single chemical idea. If the committee splits, a two-part prize pairing the two is worth testing.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine deaminase fusion work is enough to require a shared credit or a narrower citation for base editing.
Whether clinical outcomes by 2026 are strong enough to make base editing mature rather than premature.
Whether the committee prefers one broad achievement (B066) over a narrower and newer one, given that B066 has more total support but no approved PROTAC.
How to cut the eight credited names for B066 into a defensible three, particularly Deshaies versus Ciulli, and whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one achievement.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My dNTP and genome-stability work is thematically adjacent to base editing (nucleotide deamination and DNA repair), but I have no stated collaboration with the credited candidates. Collaborators named in my profile (Stillman, Rothstein, Thelander lineage) are not on the shortlist.
